new_entities.name: Lactobacillus reuteri in breastfeeding dyads
aliases: maternal L. reuteri supplementation during lactation
new_entities.description: Maternal or breastfeeding-dyad supplementation with Lactobacillus reuteri during late pregnancy or lactation.

new_entities.name: Maternal iron status
new_entities.description: Maternal iron-related status during lactation, including breast-milk iron concentration or closely related iron-availability measures.

edges.population: pregnant or lactating women, and breastfed mother-infant dyads receiving probiotic supplementation
edges.mechanism: Any iron-related effect would likely be indirect through gut or breast-milk microbiology, inflammatory signaling, or micronutrient handling during lactation rather than a direct strain-specific iron action.
edges.summary: This is mostly an evidence-gap edge. The literature on L. reuteri in breastfeeding women focuses on breast-milk immune markers and neonatal microbiota, while direct iron-status outcomes are scarce and come mainly from broader synbiotic rather than clearly strain-specific studies.
edges.caveats: The closest mineral study is synbiotic rather than clearly L. reuteri-only. This payload exists to capture uncertainty transparently, not to make a confident claim that L. reuteri improves maternal iron status.

evidence.citation: MahdaviR et al 2015 J Trace Elem Med Biol
evidence.notes: A pilot study of synbiotic supplementation on breast milk mineral concentrations and growth of exclusively breast fed infants.
Effect of Supplementation with Lactobacillus reuteri SGL 01 in Lactating Women on Breast Milk and Neonatal Gut Microbiota: An Exploratory, Randomized, Open-Label Clinical Trial.

evidence.citation: BottcherMF et al 2008 Pediatr Allergy Immunol
evidence.notes: Low breast milk TGF-beta2 is induced by Lactobacillus reuteri supplementation and associates with reduced risk of sensitization during infancy.
